slum_pulse — events per neighborhood (ชุมชน)

slum_pulse methodology

Social-signal layer geolocating news, official complaints and public social media to Bangkok's 1,993 BMA-registered communities (626 slums). 92-day rolling window.

Step 1 — Gazetteer (name-matching dictionary)

Thai name variants built from the official BMA community polygons: full and prefix-stripped slum names, landmarks (canals, roads, temples) mined from the address and N/S/E/W adjacency text, khwaeng and district names, 46 romanized district names (geoBoundaries ADM2 spatial match) and 37 famous-area aliases (Sukhumvit, Khaosan, Klong Toey…). 5,120 variants over 626 slums.

Step 2 — Official complaints (Traffy Fondue)

Pin-level citizen reports from the public share API; GPS coordinates joined directly to community polygons (no text matching needed). Limit: the public endpoint exposes only a rolling ~100-report sample of ~550; the full traffy360 dataset requires a free API token.

Step 3 — Official statistics (gdcatalog)

Crime cases, crime arrests, drug cases and corrections statistics downloaded as CSV from the Thai government open-data catalog. Province-level granularity: used as calibration denominators, not pinned to communities.

Step 4 — News ingestion

RSS feeds (Thairath, Sanook, Prachatai) plus 158 Google News RSS queries (one per khwaeng, top-40 slums by population). Article links resolved where robots.txt allows; Google News items remain snippet-only (JavaScript redirects). Headlines carry the location signal in Thai local reporting.

Step 5 — Social media

Pantip public search threads and Telegram public channel previews (t.me/s/), Thai-language channels prioritized (Thai script matches the gazetteer). Telegram policy: only channels with 5,000+ verified followers, with an exemption for Thai-language channels; subscriber counts cross-checked against independent crawlers because t.me serves decoy counts to scrapers.

Step 6 — Event extraction

Open-source Thai NLP (pythainlp tokenization) plus a keyword lexicon classifying texts into six categories: natural disaster, technical disaster, traffic incident, crime, street retail & popup markets, begging & homelessness. Thai texts machine-translated to English for display (DeepSeek, batch).

Step 7 — Geolocation tiers

T1 slum name + khwaeng/district both in text (0.9) · T2 slum name alone (0.7) · T3 khwaeng/district only, distributed across its slums by population share (0.4) · T4 landmark only (0.3). Known limit: headlines rarely name slums directly, so T3 dominates; slum-level precision comes from Traffy GPS pins.

Step 8 — Aggregation & map

Weighted event counts per community; color intensity = event count (sqrt-scaled, 50% max opacity); white = no events. BMA risk-area registry (fiscal year 2568) overlaid as reference pins. Grey-tone OSM basemap.
